from .. import *
from ..lib import wiring
from ..lib.wiring import In, Out
from .. import tracer


__all__ = ["Pin"]


class Pin(wiring.PureInterface):
    """
    An interface to an I/O buffer or a group of them that provides uniform access to input, output,
    or tristate buffers that may include a 1:n gearbox. (A 1:2 gearbox is typically called "DDR".)

    This is an interface object using :class:`Pin.Signature` as its signature.  The signature flows
    are defined from the point of view of a component that drives the I/O buffer.

    Parameters
    ----------
    width : int
        Width of the ``i``/``iN`` and ``o``/``oN`` signals.
    dir : ``"i"``, ``"o"``, ``"io"``, ``"oe"``
        Direction of the buffers. If ``"i"`` is specified, only the ``i``/``iN`` signals are
        present. If ``"o"`` is specified, only the ``o``/``oN`` signals are present. If ``"oe"`` is
        specified, the ``o``/``oN`` signals are present, and an ``oe`` signal is present.
        If ``"io"`` is specified, both the ``i``/``iN`` and ``o``/``oN`` signals are present, and
        an ``oe`` signal is present.
    xdr : int
        Gearbox ratio. If equal to 0, the I/O buffer is combinatorial, and only ``i``/``o``
        signals are present. If equal to 1, the I/O buffer is SDR, and only ``i``/``o`` signals are
        present. If greater than 1, the I/O buffer includes a gearbox, and ``iN``/``oN`` signals
        are present instead, where ``N in range(0, N)``. For example, if ``xdr=2``, the I/O buffer
        is DDR; the signal ``i0`` reflects the value at the rising edge, and the signal ``i1``
        reflects the value at the falling edge.
    path : tuple of str
        As in :class:`PureInterface`, used to name the created signals.

    Attributes
    ----------
    i_clk:
        I/O buffer input clock. Synchronizes `i*`. Present if ``xdr`` is nonzero.
    i_fclk:
        I/O buffer input fast clock. Synchronizes `i*` on higher gearbox ratios. Present if ``xdr``
        is greater than 2.
    i : Signal, out
        I/O buffer input, without gearing. Present if ``dir="i"`` or ``dir="io"``, and ``xdr`` is
        equal to 0 or 1.
    i0, i1, ... : Signal, out
        I/O buffer inputs, with gearing. Present if ``dir="i"`` or ``dir="io"``, and ``xdr`` is
        greater than 1.
    o_clk:
        I/O buffer output clock. Synchronizes `o*`, including `oe`. Present if ``xdr`` is nonzero.
    o_fclk:
        I/O buffer output fast clock. Synchronizes `o*` on higher gearbox ratios. Present if
        ``xdr`` is greater than 2.
    o : Signal, in
        I/O buffer output, without gearing. Present if ``dir="o"`` or ``dir="io"``, and ``xdr`` is
        equal to 0 or 1.
    o0, o1, ... : Signal, in
        I/O buffer outputs, with gearing. Present if ``dir="o"`` or ``dir="io"``, and ``xdr`` is
        greater than 1.
    oe : Signal, in
        I/O buffer output enable. Present if ``dir="io"`` or ``dir="oe"``. Buffers generally
        cannot change direction more than once per cycle, so at most one output enable signal
        is present.
    """

    class Signature(wiring.Signature):
        """A signature for :class:`Pin`.  The parameters are as defined on the ``Pin`` class,
        and are accessible as attributes.
        """
        def __init__(self, width, dir, *, xdr=0):
            if not isinstance(width, int) or width < 0:
                raise TypeError("Width must be a non-negative integer, not {!r}"
                                .format(width))
            if dir not in ("i", "o", "oe", "io"):
                raise TypeError("Direction must be one of \"i\", \"o\", \"io\", or \"oe\", not {!r}"""
                                .format(dir))
            if not isinstance(xdr, int) or xdr < 0:
                raise TypeError("Gearing ratio must be a non-negative integer, not {!r}"
                                .format(xdr))

            self.width = width
            self.dir = dir
            self.xdr = xdr

            members = {}
            if dir in ("i", "io"):
                if xdr > 0:
                    members["i_clk"] = Out(1)
                if xdr > 2:
                    members["i_fclk"] = Out(1)
                if xdr in (0, 1):
                    members["i"] = In(width)
                else:
                    for n in range(xdr):
                        members[f"i{n}"] = In(width)
            if dir in ("o", "oe", "io"):
                if xdr > 0:
                    members["o_clk"] = Out(1)
                if xdr > 2:
                    members["o_fclk"] = Out(1)
                if xdr in (0, 1):
                    members["o"] = Out(width)
                else:
                    for n in range(xdr):
                        members[f"o{n}"] = Out(width)
            if dir in ("oe", "io"):
                members["oe"] = Out(1)
            super().__init__(members)

        def __eq__(self, other):
            return (type(self) is type(other) and
                    self.width == other.width and
                    self.dir == other.dir and
                    self.xdr == other.xdr)

        def __repr__(self):
            xdr = f", xdr={self.xdr}" if self.xdr != 0 else ""
            return f"Pin.Signature({self.width}, dir={self.dir!r}{xdr})"

        def create(self, *, path=None, src_loc_at=0):
            return Pin(self.width, self.dir, xdr=self.xdr, path=path, src_loc_at=1 + src_loc_at)

    def __init__(self, width, dir, *, xdr=0, name=None, path=None, src_loc_at=0):
        if name is not None:
            if path is not None:
                raise ValueError("Cannot pass both name and path")
            path = (name,)
        if path is None:
            name = tracer.get_var_name(depth=2 + src_loc_at, default="$pin")
            path = (name,)
        self.path = tuple(path)
        self.name = "__".join(path)
        signature = Pin.Signature(width, dir, xdr=xdr)
        super().__init__(signature, path=path, src_loc_at=src_loc_at + 1)

    @property
    def width(self):
        return self.signature.width

    @property
    def dir(self):
        return self.signature.dir

    @property
    def xdr(self):
        return self.signature.xdr

82: class Layout(ShapeCastable, metaclass=ABCMeta):
83:     """Description of a data layout.
84: 
85:     The :ref:`shape-like <lang-shapelike>` :class:`Layout` interface associates keys
86:     (string names or integer indexes) with fields, giving identifiers to spans of bits in
87:     an Amaranth value.
88: 
89:     It is an abstract base class; :class:`StructLayout`, :class:`UnionLayout`,
90:     :class:`ArrayLayout`, and :class:`FlexibleLayout` implement concrete layout rules.
91:     New layout rules can be defined by inheriting from this class.
92: 
93:     Like all other shape-castable objects, all layouts are immutable. New classes deriving from
94:     :class:`Layout` must preserve this invariant.
95:     """
96: 
97:     @staticmethod
98:     def cast(obj):
99:         """Cast a :ref:`shape-like <lang-shapelike>` object to a layout.
100: 
101:         This method performs a subset of the operations done by :meth:`Shape.cast`; it will
102:         recursively call ``.as_shape()``, but only until a layout is returned.
103: 
104:         Raises
105:         ------
106:         TypeError
107:             If ``obj`` cannot be converted to a :class:`Layout` instance.
108:         RecursionError
109:             If ``obj.as_shape()`` returns ``obj``.
110:         """
111:         while isinstance(obj, ShapeCastable):
112:             if isinstance(obj, Layout):
113:                 return obj
114:             new_obj = obj.as_shape()
115:             if new_obj is obj:
116:                 break
117:             obj = new_obj
118:         Shape.cast(obj) # delegate non-layout-specific error handling to Shape
119:         raise TypeError("Object {!r} cannot be converted to a data layout"
120:                         .format(obj))
121: 
122:     @abstractmethod
123:     def __iter__(self):
124:         """Iterate fields in the layout.
125: 
126:         Yields
127:         ------
128:         :class:`str` or :class:`int`
129:             Key (either name or index) for accessing the field.
130:         :class:`Field`
131:             Description of the field.
132:         """
133: 
134:     @abstractmethod
135:     def __getitem__(self, key):
136:         """Retrieve a field from the layout.
137: 
138:         Returns
139:         -------
140:         :class:`Field`
141:             The field associated with ``key``.
142: 
143:         Raises
144:         ------
145:         KeyError
146:             If there is no field associated with ``key``.
147:         """
148: 
149:     @property
150:     @abstractmethod
151:     def size(self):
152:         """Size of the layout.
153: 
154:         Returns
155:         -------
156:         :class:`int`
157:             The amount of bits required to store every field in the layout.
158:         """
159: 
160:     def as_shape(self):
161:         """Shape of the layout.
162: 
163:         Returns
164:         -------
165:         :class:`Shape`
166:             ``unsigned(self.size)``
167:         """
168:         return unsigned(self.size)
169: 
170:     def __eq__(self, other):
171:         """Compare layouts.
172: 
173:         Two layouts are equal if they have the same size and the same fields under the same names.
174:         The order of the fields is not considered.
175:         """
176:         while isinstance(other, ShapeCastable) and not isinstance(other, Layout):
177:             new_other = other.as_shape()
178:             if new_other is other:
179:                 break
180:             other = new_other
181:         return (isinstance(other, Layout) and self.size == other.size and
182:                 dict(iter(self)) == dict(iter(other)))
183: 
184:     def __call__(self, target):
185:         """Create a view into a target.
186: 
187:         When a :class:`Layout` is used as the shape of a :class:`Field` and accessed through
188:         a :class:`View`, this method is used to wrap the slice of the underlying value into
189:         another view with this layout.
190: 
191:         Returns
192:         -------
193:         :class:`View`
194:             ``View(self, target)``
195:         """
196:         return View(self, target)
197: 
198:     def const(self, init):
199:         """Convert a constant initializer to a constant.
200: 
201:         Converts ``init``, which may be a sequence or a mapping of field values, to a constant.
202: 
203:         Returns
204:         -------
205:         :class:`Const`
206:             A constant that has the same value as a view with this layout that was initialized with
207:             an all-zero value and had every field assigned to the corresponding value in the order
208:             in which they appear in ``init``.
209:         """
210:         if init is None:
211:             iterator = iter(())
212:         elif isinstance(init, Mapping):
213:             iterator = init.items()
214:         elif isinstance(init, Sequence):
215:             iterator = enumerate(init)
216:         else:
217:             raise TypeError("Layout constant initializer must be a mapping or a sequence, not {!r}"
218:                             .format(init))
219: 
220:         int_value = 0
221:         for key, key_value in iterator:
222:             field = self[key]
223:             cast_field_shape = Shape.cast(field.shape)
224:             if isinstance(field.shape, ShapeCastable):
225:                 key_value = Const.cast(field.shape.const(key_value))
226:                 if key_value.shape() != cast_field_shape:
227:                     raise ValueError("Constant returned by {!r}.const() must have the shape that "
228:                                      "it casts to, {!r}, and not {!r}"
229:                                      .format(field.shape, cast_field_shape,
230:                                              key_value.shape()))
231:             elif not isinstance(key_value, Const):
232:                 key_value = Const(key_value, cast_field_shape)
233:             mask = ((1 << cast_field_shape.width) - 1) << field.offset
234:             int_value &= ~mask
235:             int_value |= (key_value.value << field.offset) & mask
236:         return View(self, Const(int_value, self.as_shape()))
237: 
238:     def __int__(self):
239:         """Convert layout to integer (size of the layout)."""
240:         return self.size
241: 
242:     def _value_repr(self, value):
243:         yield Repr(FormatInt(), value)
244:         for key, field in self:
245:             shape = Shape.cast(field.shape)
246:             field_value = value[field.offset:field.offset+shape.width]
247:             if shape.signed:
248:                 field_value = field_value.as_signed()
249:             if isinstance(field.shape, ShapeCastable):
250:                 for repr in field.shape._value_repr(field_value):
251:                     yield Repr(repr.format, repr.value, path=(key,) + repr.path)
252:             elif isinstance(field.shape, type) and issubclass(field.shape, Enum):
253:                 yield Repr(FormatEnum(field.shape), field_value, path=(key,))
254:             else:
255:                 yield Repr(FormatInt(), field_value, path=(key,))

258: class StructLayout(Layout):
259:     """Description of a structure layout.
260: 
261:     The fields of a structure layout follow one another without any gaps, and the size of
262:     a structure layout is the sum of the sizes of its members.
263: 
264:     For example, the following layout of a 16-bit value:
265: 
266:     .. image:: _images/data/struct_layout.svg
267: 
268:     can be described with:
269: 
270:     .. testcode::
271: 
272:         data.StructLayout({
273:             "first":  3,
274:             "second": 7,
275:             "third":  6
276:         })
277: 
278:     .. note::
279: 
280:         Structures that have padding can be described with a :class:`FlexibleLayout`. Alternately,
281:         padding can be added to the layout as fields called ``_1``, ``_2``, and so on. These fields
282:         won't be accessible as attributes or by using indexing.
283: 
284:     Attributes
285:     ----------
286:     members : mapping of :class:`str` to :ref:`shape-like <lang-shapelike>`
287:         Dictionary of structure members.
288:     """
289: 
290:     def __init__(self, members):
291:         offset = 0
292:         self._fields = {}
293:         if not isinstance(members, Mapping):
294:             raise TypeError("Struct layout members must be provided as a mapping, not {!r}"
295:                             .format(members))
296:         for key, shape in members.items():
297:             if not isinstance(key, str):
298:                 raise TypeError("Struct layout member name must be a string, not {!r}"
299:                                 .format(key))
300:             try:
301:                 cast_shape = Shape.cast(shape)
302:             except TypeError as e:
303:                 raise TypeError("Struct layout member shape must be a shape-castable object, "
304:                                 "not {!r}"
305:                                 .format(shape)) from e
306:             self._fields[key] = Field(shape, offset)
307:             offset += cast_shape.width
308: 
309:     @property
310:     def members(self):
311:         return {key: field.shape for key, field in self._fields.items()}
312: 
313:     def __iter__(self):
314:         return iter(self._fields.items())
315: 
316:     def __getitem__(self, key):
317:         return self._fields[key]
318: 
319:     @property
320:     def size(self):
321:         """Size of the structure layout.
322: 
323:         Returns
324:         -------
325:         :class:`int`
326:             Index of the most significant bit of the *last* field plus one; or zero if there are
327:             no fields.
328:         """
329:         return max((field.offset + field.width for field in self._fields.values()), default=0)
330: 
331:     def __repr__(self):
332:         return f"StructLayout({self.members!r})"
333:

336:     """Description of a union layout.
337: 
338:     The fields of a union layout all start from bit 0, and the size of a union layout is the size
339:     of the largest of its members.
340: 
341:     For example, the following layout of a 7-bit value:
342: 
343:     .. image:: _images/data/union_layout.svg
344: 
345:     can be described with:
346: 
347:     .. testcode::
348: 
349:         data.UnionLayout({
350:             "first":  3,
351:             "second": 7,
352:             "third":  6
353:         })
354: 
355:     Attributes
356:     ----------
357:     members : mapping of :class:`str` to :ref:`shape-like <lang-shapelike>`
358:         Dictionary of union members.
359:     """
360:     def __init__(self, members):
361:         self._fields = {}
362:         if not isinstance(members, Mapping):
363:             raise TypeError("Union layout members must be provided as a mapping, not {!r}"
364:                             .format(members))
365:         for key, shape in members.items():
366:             if not isinstance(key, str):
367:                 raise TypeError("Union layout member name must be a string, not {!r}"
368:                                 .format(key))
369:             try:
370:                 cast_shape = Shape.cast(shape)
371:             except TypeError as e:
372:                 raise TypeError("Union layout member shape must be a shape-castable object, "
373:                                 "not {!r}"
374:                                 .format(shape)) from e
375:             self._fields[key] = Field(shape, 0)
376: 
377:     @property
378:     def members(self):
379:         return {key: field.shape for key, field in self._fields.items()}
380: 
381:     def __iter__(self):
382:         return iter(self._fields.items())
383: 
384:     def __getitem__(self, key):
385:         return self._fields[key]
386: 
387:     @property
388:     def size(self):
389:         """Size of the union layout.
390: 
391:         Returns
392:         -------
393:         :class:`int`
394:             Index of the most significant bit of the *largest* field plus one; or zero if there are
395:             no fields.
396:         """
397:         return max((field.width for field in self._fields.values()), default=0)

399:     def const(self, init):

410: class ArrayLayout(Layout):
411:     """Description of an array layout.
412: 
413:     The fields of an array layout follow one another without any gaps, and the size of an array
414:     layout is the size of its element multiplied by its length.
415: 
416:     For example, the following layout of a 16-bit value:
417: 
418:     .. image:: _images/data/array_layout.svg
419: 
420:     can be described with:
421: 
422:     .. testcode::
423: 
424:         data.ArrayLayout(unsigned(4), 4)
425: 
426:     .. note::
427: 
428:         Arrays that have padding can be described with a :class:`FlexibleLayout`.
429: 
430:     Attributes
431:     ----------
432:     elem_shape : :ref:`shape-like <lang-shapelike>`
433:         Shape of an individual element.
434:     length : :class:`int`
435:         Amount of elements.
436:     """
437:     def __init__(self, elem_shape, length):
438:         try:
439:             Shape.cast(elem_shape)
440:         except TypeError as e:
441:             raise TypeError("Array layout element shape must be a shape-castable object, "
442:                             "not {!r}"
443:                             .format(elem_shape)) from e
444:         if not isinstance(length, int) or length < 0:
445:             raise TypeError("Array layout length must be a non-negative integer, not {!r}"
446:                             .format(length))
447:         self._elem_shape = elem_shape
448:         self._length     = length
449: 
450:     @property
451:     def elem_shape(self):
452:         return self._elem_shape
453: 
454:     @property
455:     def length(self):
456:         return self._length
457: 
458:     def __iter__(self):
459:         offset = 0
460:         for index in range(self._length):
461:             yield index, Field(self._elem_shape, offset)
462:             offset += Shape.cast(self._elem_shape).width
463: 
464:     def __getitem__(self, key):
465:         if isinstance(key, int):
466:             if key not in range(-self._length, self._length):
467:                 # Layout's interface requires us to raise KeyError, not IndexError
468:                 raise KeyError(key)
469:             if key < 0:
470:                 key += self._length
471:             return Field(self._elem_shape, key * Shape.cast(self._elem_shape).width)
472:         raise TypeError(f"Cannot index array layout with {key!r}")
473: 
474:     @property
475:     def size(self):
476:         """Size of the array layout.
477: 
478:         Returns
479:         -------
480:         :class:`int`
481:             Size of an individual element multiplied by their amount.
482:         """
483:         return Shape.cast(self._elem_shape).width * self.length
484: 
485:     def __repr__(self):
486:         return f"ArrayLayout({self._elem_shape!r}, {self.length})"
487:

489: class FlexibleLayout(Layout):
490:     """Description of a flexible layout.
491: 
492:     A flexible layout is similar to a structure layout; while fields in :class:`StructLayout` are
493:     defined contiguously, the fields in a flexible layout can overlap and have gaps between them.
494: 
495:     Because the size and field boundaries in a flexible layout can be defined arbitrarily, it
496:     may also be more convenient to use a flexible layout when the layout information is derived
497:     from an external data file rather than defined in Python code.
498: 
499:     For example, the following layout of a 16-bit value:
500: 
501:     .. image:: _images/data/flexible_layout.svg
502: 
503:     can be described with:
504: 
505:     .. testcode::
506: 
507:         data.FlexibleLayout(16, {
508:             "first":  data.Field(unsigned(3), 1),
509:             "second": data.Field(unsigned(7), 0),
510:             "third":  data.Field(unsigned(6), 10),
511:             0:        data.Field(unsigned(1), 14)
512:         })
513: 
514:     Both strings and integers can be used as names of flexible layout fields, so flexible layouts
515:     can be used to describe structures with arbitrary padding and arrays with arbitrary stride.
516: 
517:     If another data structure is used as the source of truth for creating flexible layouts,
518:     consider instead inheriting from the base :class:`Layout` class, which may be more convenient.
519: 
520:     Attributes
521:     ----------
522:     size : :class:`int`
523:         Size of the layout.
524:     fields : mapping of :class:`str` or :class:`int` to :class:`Field`
525:         Fields defined in the layout.
526:     """
527:     def __init__(self, size, fields):
528:         if not isinstance(size, int) or size < 0:
529:             raise TypeError("Flexible layout size must be a non-negative integer, not {!r}"
530:                             .format(size))
531:         if not isinstance(fields, Mapping):
532:             raise TypeError("Flexible layout fields must be provided as a mapping, not {!r}"
533:                             .format(fields))
534:         self._size = size
535:         self._fields = {}
536:         for key, field in fields.items():
537:             if not isinstance(key, (int, str)) or (isinstance(key, int) and key < 0):
538:                 raise TypeError("Flexible layout field name must be a non-negative integer or "
539:                                 "a string, not {!r}"
540:                                 .format(key))
541:             if not isinstance(field, Field):
542:                 raise TypeError("Flexible layout field value must be a Field instance, not {!r}"
543:                                 .format(field))
544:             if field.offset + field.width > size:
545:                 raise ValueError("Flexible layout field '{}' ends at bit {}, exceeding "
546:                                  "the size of {} bit(s)"
547:                                  .format(key, field.offset + field.width, size))
548:             self._fields[key] = field
549: 
550:     @property
551:     def size(self):
552:         """:meta private:""" # work around Sphinx bug
553:         return self._size
554: 
555:     @property
556:     def fields(self):
557:         return {**self._fields}
558: 
559:     def __iter__(self):
560:         return iter(self._fields.items())
561: 
562:     def __getitem__(self, key):
563:         if isinstance(key, (int, str)):
564:             return self._fields[key]
565:         raise TypeError(f"Cannot index flexible layout with {key!r}")
566: 
567:     def __repr__(self):
568:         return f"FlexibleLayout({self._size}, {self._fields!r})"

571: class View(ValueCastable):
572:     """A value viewed through the lens of a layout.
573: 
574:     The :ref:`value-like <lang-valuelike>` class :class:`View` provides access to the fields
575:     of an underlying Amaranth value via the names or indexes defined in the provided layout.
576: 
577:     Creating a view
578:     ###############
579: 
580:     A view must be created using an explicitly provided layout and target. To create a new :class:`Signal` that is wrapped in a :class:`View` with a given ``layout``, use ``Signal(layout, ...)``, which for a :class:`Layout` is equivalent to ``View(layout, Signal(...))``.
581: 
582:     Accessing a view
583:     ################
584: 
585:     Slicing a view or accessing its attributes returns a part of the underlying value
586:     corresponding to the field with that index or name, which is itself either a value or
587:     a value-castable object. If the shape of the field is a :class:`Layout`, it will be
588:     a :class:`View`; if it is a class deriving from :class:`Struct` or :class:`Union`, it
589:     will be an instance of that data class; if it is another
590:     :ref:`shape-like <lang-shapelike>` object implementing ``__call__``, it will be
591:     the result of calling that method.
592: 
593:     Slicing a view whose layout is an :class:`ArrayLayout` can be done with an index that is
594:     an Amaranth value instead of a constant integer. The returned element is chosen dynamically
595:     in that case.
596: 
597:     A view can only be compared for equality with another view of the same layout,
598:     returning a single-bit value. No other operators are supported on views. If required,
599:     a view can be converted back to its underlying value via :meth:`as_value`.
600: 
601:     Custom view classes
602:     ###################
603: 
604:     The :class:`View` class can be inherited from to define additional properties or methods on
605:     a view. The only two names that are reserved on instances of :class:`View` are :meth:`as_value`
606:     and :meth:`eq`, leaving the rest to the developer. The :class:`Struct` and :class:`Union`
607:     classes provided in this module are subclasses of :class:`View` that also provide a concise way
608:     to define a layout.
609:     """
610:     def __init__(self, layout, target):
611:         try:
612:             cast_layout = Layout.cast(layout)
613:         except TypeError as e:
614:             raise TypeError("View layout must be a layout, not {!r}"
615:                             .format(layout)) from e
616:         try:
617:             cast_target = Value.cast(target)
618:         except TypeError as e:
619:             raise TypeError("View target must be a value-castable object, not {!r}"
620:                             .format(target)) from e
621:         if len(cast_target) != cast_layout.size:
622:             raise ValueError("View target is {} bit(s) wide, which is not compatible with "
623:                              "the {} bit(s) wide view layout"
624:                              .format(len(cast_target), cast_layout.size))
625:         for name, field in cast_layout:
626:             if isinstance(name, str) and name[0] != "_" and hasattr(type(self), name):
627:                 warnings.warn("View layout includes a field {!r} that will be shadowed by "
628:                               "the view attribute '{}.{}.{}'"
629:                               .format(name, type(self).__module__, type(self).__qualname__, name),
630:                               SyntaxWarning, stacklevel=2)
631:         self.__orig_layout = layout
632:         self.__layout = cast_layout
633:         self.__target = cast_target
634: 
635:     def shape(self):
636:         """Get layout of this view.
637: 
638:         Returns
639:         -------
640:         :class:`Layout`
641:             The ``layout`` provided when constructing the view.
642:         """
643:         return self.__orig_layout
644: 
645:     def as_value(self):
646:         """Get underlying value.
647: 
648:         Returns
649:         -------
650:         :class:`Value`
651:             The ``target`` provided when constructing the view, or the :class:`Signal` that
652:             was created.
653:         """
654:         return self.__target
655: 
656:     def eq(self, other):
657:         """Assign to the underlying value.
658: 
659:         Returns
660:         -------
661:         :class:`Assign`
662:             ``self.as_value().eq(other)``
663:         """
664:         return self.as_value().eq(other)
665: 
666:     def __getitem__(self, key):
667:         """Slice the underlying value.
668: 
669:         A field corresponding to ``key`` is looked up in the layout. If the field's shape is
670:         a shape-castable object that has a ``__call__`` method, it is called and the result is
671:         returned. Otherwise, ``as_shape`` is called repeatedly on the shape until either an object
672:         with a ``__call__`` method is reached, or a ``Shape`` is returned. In the latter case,
673:         returns an unspecified Amaranth expression with the right shape.
674: 
675:         Arguments
676:         ---------
677:         key : :class:`str` or :class:`int` or :class:`ValueCastable`
678:             Name or index of a field.
679: 
680:         Returns
681:         -------
682:         :class:`Value` or :class:`ValueCastable`, inout
683:             A slice of the underlying value defined by the field.
684: 
685:         Raises
686:         ------
687:         KeyError
688:             If the layout does not define a field corresponding to ``key``.
689:         TypeError
690:             If ``key`` is a value-castable object, but the layout of the view is not
691:             a :class:`ArrayLayout`.
692:         TypeError
693:             If ``ShapeCastable.__call__`` does not return a value or a value-castable object.
694:         """
695:         if isinstance(self.__layout, ArrayLayout):
696:             if not isinstance(key, (int, Value, ValueCastable)):
697:                 raise TypeError("Views with array layout may only be indexed with an integer "
698:                                 "or a value, not {!r}"
699:                                 .format(key))

701:             value = self.__target.word_select(key, Shape.cast(self.__layout.elem_shape).width)

from abc import ABCMeta, abstractmethod
from enum import Enum
from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
import warnings

from amaranth._utils import final
from amaranth.hdl import *
from amaranth.hdl._repr import *
from amaranth.hdl._ast import ShapeCastable, ValueCastable


__all__ = [
    "Field", "Layout", "StructLayout", "UnionLayout", "ArrayLayout", "FlexibleLayout",
    "View", "Struct", "Union",
]


@final
class Field:
    """Description of a data field.

    The :class:`Field` class specifies the signedness and bit positions of a field in
    an Amaranth value.

    :class:`Field` objects are immutable.

    Attributes
    ----------
    shape : :ref:`shape-like <lang-shapelike>`
        Shape of the field. When initialized or assigned, the object is stored as-is.
    offset : :class:`int`, >=0
        Index of the least significant bit of the field.
    """
    def __init__(self, shape, offset):
        try:
            Shape.cast(shape)
        except TypeError as e:
            raise TypeError("Field shape must be a shape-castable object, not {!r}"
                            .format(shape)) from e
        if not isinstance(offset, int) or offset < 0:
            raise TypeError("Field offset must be a non-negative integer, not {!r}"
                            .format(offset))
        self._shape  = shape
        self._offset = offset

    @property
    def shape(self):
        return self._shape

    @property
    def offset(self):
        return self._offset

    @property
    def width(self):
        """Width of the field.

        This property should be used over ``self.shape.width`` because ``self.shape`` can be
        an arbitrary :ref:`shape-like <lang-shapelike>` object, which may not have
        a ``width`` property.

        Returns
        -------
        :class:`int`
            ``Shape.cast(self.shape).width``
        """
        return Shape.cast(self.shape).width

    def __eq__(self, other):
        """Compare fields.

        Two fields are equal if they have the same shape and offset.
        """
        return (isinstance(other, Field) and
                Shape.cast(self._shape) == Shape.cast(other.shape) and
                self._offset == other.offset)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"Field({self._shape!r}, {self._offset})"


class Layout(ShapeCastable, metaclass=ABCMeta):
    """Description of a data layout.

    The :ref:`shape-like <lang-shapelike>` :class:`Layout` interface associates keys
    (string names or integer indexes) with fields, giving identifiers to spans of bits in
    an Amaranth value.

    It is an abstract base class; :class:`StructLayout`, :class:`UnionLayout`,
    :class:`ArrayLayout`, and :class:`FlexibleLayout` implement concrete layout rules.
    New layout rules can be defined by inheriting from this class.

    Like all other shape-castable objects, all layouts are immutable. New classes deriving from
    :class:`Layout` must preserve this invariant.
    """

    @staticmethod
    def cast(obj):
        """Cast a :ref:`shape-like <lang-shapelike>` object to a layout.

        This method performs a subset of the operations done by :meth:`Shape.cast`; it will
        recursively call ``.as_shape()``, but only until a layout is returned.

        Raises
        ------
        TypeError
            If ``obj`` cannot be converted to a :class:`Layout` instance.
        RecursionError
            If ``obj.as_shape()`` returns ``obj``.
        """
        while isinstance(obj, ShapeCastable):
            if isinstance(obj, Layout):
                return obj
            new_obj = obj.as_shape()
            if new_obj is obj:
                break
            obj = new_obj
        Shape.cast(obj) # delegate non-layout-specific error handling to Shape
        raise TypeError("Object {!r} cannot be converted to a data layout"
                        .format(obj))

    @abstractmethod
    def __iter__(self):
        """Iterate fields in the layout.

        Yields
        ------
        :class:`str` or :class:`int`
            Key (either name or index) for accessing the field.
        :class:`Field`
            Description of the field.
        """

    @abstractmethod
    def __getitem__(self, key):
        """Retrieve a field from the layout.

        Returns
        -------
        :class:`Field`
            The field associated with ``key``.

        Raises
        ------
        KeyError
            If there is no field associated with ``key``.
        """

    @property
    @abstractmethod
    def size(self):
        """Size of the layout.

        Returns
        -------
        :class:`int`
            The amount of bits required to store every field in the layout.
        """

    def as_shape(self):
        """Shape of the layout.

        Returns
        -------
        :class:`Shape`
            ``unsigned(self.size)``
        """
        return unsigned(self.size)

    def __eq__(self, other):
        """Compare layouts.

        Two layouts are equal if they have the same size and the same fields under the same names.
        The order of the fields is not considered.
        """
        while isinstance(other, ShapeCastable) and not isinstance(other, Layout):
            new_other = other.as_shape()
            if new_other is other:
                break
            other = new_other
        return (isinstance(other, Layout) and self.size == other.size and
                dict(iter(self)) == dict(iter(other)))

    def __call__(self, target):
        """Create a view into a target.

        When a :class:`Layout` is used as the shape of a :class:`Field` and accessed through
        a :class:`View`, this method is used to wrap the slice of the underlying value into
        another view with this layout.

        Returns
        -------
        :class:`View`
            ``View(self, target)``
        """
        return View(self, target)

    def const(self, init):
        """Convert a constant initializer to a constant.

        Converts ``init``, which may be a sequence or a mapping of field values, to a constant.

        Returns
        -------
        :class:`Const`
            A constant that has the same value as a view with this layout that was initialized with
            an all-zero value and had every field assigned to the corresponding value in the order
            in which they appear in ``init``.
        """
        if init is None:
            iterator = iter(())
        elif isinstance(init, Mapping):
            iterator = init.items()
        elif isinstance(init, Sequence):
            iterator = enumerate(init)
        else:
            raise TypeError("Layout constant initializer must be a mapping or a sequence, not {!r}"
                            .format(init))

        int_value = 0
        for key, key_value in iterator:
            field = self[key]
            cast_field_shape = Shape.cast(field.shape)
            if isinstance(field.shape, ShapeCastable):
                key_value = Const.cast(field.shape.const(key_value))
                if key_value.shape() != cast_field_shape:
                    raise ValueError("Constant returned by {!r}.const() must have the shape that "
                                     "it casts to, {!r}, and not {!r}"
                                     .format(field.shape, cast_field_shape,
                                             key_value.shape()))
            elif not isinstance(key_value, Const):
                key_value = Const(key_value, cast_field_shape)
            mask = ((1 << cast_field_shape.width) - 1) << field.offset
            int_value &= ~mask
            int_value |= (key_value.value << field.offset) & mask
        return View(self, Const(int_value, self.as_shape()))

    def __int__(self):
        """Convert layout to integer (size of the layout)."""
        return self.size

    def _value_repr(self, value):
        yield Repr(FormatInt(), value)
        for key, field in self:
            shape = Shape.cast(field.shape)
            field_value = value[field.offset:field.offset+shape.width]
            if shape.signed:
                field_value = field_value.as_signed()
            if isinstance(field.shape, ShapeCastable):
                for repr in field.shape._value_repr(field_value):
                    yield Repr(repr.format, repr.value, path=(key,) + repr.path)
            elif isinstance(field.shape, type) and issubclass(field.shape, Enum):
                yield Repr(FormatEnum(field.shape), field_value, path=(key,))
            else:
                yield Repr(FormatInt(), field_value, path=(key,))


class StructLayout(Layout):
    """Description of a structure layout.

    The fields of a structure layout follow one another without any gaps, and the size of
    a structure layout is the sum of the sizes of its members.

    For example, the following layout of a 16-bit value:

    .. image:: _images/data/struct_layout.svg

    can be described with:

    .. testcode::

        data.StructLayout({
            "first":  3,
            "second": 7,
            "third":  6
        })

    .. note::

        Structures that have padding can be described with a :class:`FlexibleLayout`. Alternately,
        padding can be added to the layout as fields called ``_1``, ``_2``, and so on. These fields
        won't be accessible as attributes or by using indexing.

    Attributes
    ----------
    members : mapping of :class:`str` to :ref:`shape-like <lang-shapelike>`
        Dictionary of structure members.
    """

    def __init__(self, members):
        offset = 0
        self._fields = {}
        if not isinstance(members, Mapping):
            raise TypeError("Struct layout members must be provided as a mapping, not {!r}"
                            .format(members))
        for key, shape in members.items():
            if not isinstance(key, str):
                raise TypeError("Struct layout member name must be a string, not {!r}"
                                .format(key))
            try:
                cast_shape = Shape.cast(shape)
            except TypeError as e:
                raise TypeError("Struct layout member shape must be a shape-castable object, "
                                "not {!r}"
                                .format(shape)) from e
            self._fields[key] = Field(shape, offset)
            offset += cast_shape.width

    @property
    def members(self):
        return {key: field.shape for key, field in self._fields.items()}

    def __iter__(self):
        return iter(self._fields.items())

    def __getitem__(self, key):
        return self._fields[key]

    @property
    def size(self):
        """Size of the structure layout.

        Returns
        -------
        :class:`int`
            Index of the most significant bit of the *last* field plus one; or zero if there are
            no fields.
        """
        return max((field.offset + field.width for field in self._fields.values()), default=0)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"StructLayout({self.members!r})"


class UnionLayout(Layout):
    """Description of a union layout.

    The fields of a union layout all start from bit 0, and the size of a union layout is the size
    of the largest of its members.

    For example, the following layout of a 7-bit value:

    .. image:: _images/data/union_layout.svg

    can be described with:

    .. testcode::

        data.UnionLayout({
            "first":  3,
            "second": 7,
            "third":  6
        })

    Attributes
    ----------
    members : mapping of :class:`str` to :ref:`shape-like <lang-shapelike>`
        Dictionary of union members.
    """
    def __init__(self, members):
        self._fields = {}
        if not isinstance(members, Mapping):
            raise TypeError("Union layout members must be provided as a mapping, not {!r}"
                            .format(members))
        for key, shape in members.items():
            if not isinstance(key, str):
                raise TypeError("Union layout member name must be a string, not {!r}"
                                .format(key))
            try:
                cast_shape = Shape.cast(shape)
            except TypeError as e:
                raise TypeError("Union layout member shape must be a shape-castable object, "
                                "not {!r}"
                                .format(shape)) from e
            self._fields[key] = Field(shape, 0)

    @property
    def members(self):
        return {key: field.shape for key, field in self._fields.items()}

    def __iter__(self):
        return iter(self._fields.items())

    def __getitem__(self, key):
        return self._fields[key]

    @property
    def size(self):
        """Size of the union layout.

        Returns
        -------
        :class:`int`
            Index of the most significant bit of the *largest* field plus one; or zero if there are
            no fields.
        """
        return max((field.width for field in self._fields.values()), default=0)

    def const(self, init):
        if init is not None and len(init) > 1:
            raise ValueError("Initializer for at most one field can be provided for "
                             "a union layout (specified: {})"
                             .format(", ".join(init.keys())))
        return super().const(init)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"UnionLayout({self.members!r})"


class ArrayLayout(Layout):
    """Description of an array layout.

    The fields of an array layout follow one another without any gaps, and the size of an array
    layout is the size of its element multiplied by its length.

    For example, the following layout of a 16-bit value:

    .. image:: _images/data/array_layout.svg

    can be described with:

    .. testcode::

        data.ArrayLayout(unsigned(4), 4)

    .. note::

        Arrays that have padding can be described with a :class:`FlexibleLayout`.

    Attributes
    ----------
    elem_shape : :ref:`shape-like <lang-shapelike>`
        Shape of an individual element.
    length : :class:`int`
        Amount of elements.
    """
    def __init__(self, elem_shape, length):
        try:
            Shape.cast(elem_shape)
        except TypeError as e:

                            "not {!r}"
                            .format(elem_shape)) from e
        if not isinstance(length, int) or length < 0:
            raise TypeError("Array layout length must be a non-negative integer, not {!r}"
                            .format(length))

        self._length     = length

    def elem_shape(self):
        return self._elem_shape

    @property
    def length(self):
        return self._length

    def __iter__(self):

            yield index, Field(self._elem_shape, offset)
            offset += Shape.cast(self._elem_shape).width

                key += self._length

    def size(self):

        Returns
        -------
        :class:`int`
            Size of an individual element multiplied by their amount.
        """

    def __repr__(self):

class FlexibleLayout(Layout):
    """Description of a flexible layout.

    A flexible layout is similar to a structure layout; while fields in :class:`StructLayout` are
    defined contiguously, the fields in a flexible layout can overlap and have gaps between them.

    Because the size and field boundaries in a flexible layout can be defined arbitrarily, it
    may also be more convenient to use a flexible layout when the layout information is derived
    from an external data file rather than defined in Python code.

    For example, the following layout of a 16-bit value:

    .. image:: _images/data/flexible_layout.svg

    can be described with:

    .. testcode::

        data.FlexibleLayout(16, {
            "first":  data.Field(unsigned(3), 1),
            "second": data.Field(unsigned(7), 0),
            "third":  data.Field(unsigned(6), 10),
            0:        data.Field(unsigned(1), 14)
        })

    Both strings and integers can be used as names of flexible layout fields, so flexible layouts
    can be used to describe structures with arbitrary padding and arrays with arbitrary stride.

    If another data structure is used as the source of truth for creating flexible layouts,
    consider instead inheriting from the base :class:`Layout` class, which may be more convenient.

    Attributes
    ----------
    size : :class:`int`
        Size of the layout.
    fields : mapping of :class:`str` or :class:`int` to :class:`Field`
        Fields defined in the layout.
    """
    def __init__(self, size, fields):
        if not isinstance(size, int) or size < 0:
            raise TypeError("Flexible layout size must be a non-negative integer, not {!r}"
                            .format(size))
        if not isinstance(fields, Mapping):
            raise TypeError("Flexible layout fields must be provided as a mapping, not {!r}"
                            .format(fields))
        self._size = size
        self._fields = {}
        for key, field in fields.items():
            if not isinstance(key, (int, str)) or (isinstance(key, int) and key < 0):
                raise TypeError("Flexible layout field name must be a non-negative integer or "
                                "a string, not {!r}"
                                .format(key))
            if not isinstance(field, Field):
                raise TypeError("Flexible layout field value must be a Field instance, not {!r}"
                                .format(field))
            if field.offset + field.width > size:
                raise ValueError("Flexible layout field '{}' ends at bit {}, exceeding "
                                 "the size of {} bit(s)"
                                 .format(key, field.offset + field.width, size))
            self._fields[key] = field

    @property
    def size(self):
        """:meta private:""" # work around Sphinx bug
        return self._size

    @property
    def fields(self):
        return {**self._fields}

    def __iter__(self):
        return iter(self._fields.items())

    def __getitem__(self, key):
        if isinstance(key, (int, str)):
            return self._fields[key]
        raise TypeError(f"Cannot index flexible layout with {key!r}")

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"FlexibleLayout({self._size}, {self._fields!r})"


class View(ValueCastable):
    """A value viewed through the lens of a layout.

    The :ref:`value-like <lang-valuelike>` class :class:`View` provides access to the fields
    of an underlying Amaranth value via the names or indexes defined in the provided layout.

    Creating a view
    ###############

    A view must be created using an explicitly provided layout and target. To create a new :class:`Signal` that is wrapped in a :class:`View` with a given ``layout``, use ``Signal(layout, ...)``, which for a :class:`Layout` is equivalent to ``View(layout, Signal(...))``.

    Accessing a view
    ################

    Slicing a view or accessing its attributes returns a part of the underlying value
    corresponding to the field with that index or name, which is itself either a value or
    a value-castable object. If the shape of the field is a :class:`Layout`, it will be
    a :class:`View`; if it is a class deriving from :class:`Struct` or :class:`Union`, it
    will be an instance of that data class; if it is another
    :ref:`shape-like <lang-shapelike>` object implementing ``__call__``, it will be
    the result of calling that method.

    Slicing a view whose layout is an :class:`ArrayLayout` can be done with an index that is
    an Amaranth value instead of a constant integer. The returned element is chosen dynamically
    in that case.

    A view can only be compared for equality with another view of the same layout,
    returning a single-bit value. No other operators are supported on views. If required,
    a view can be converted back to its underlying value via :meth:`as_value`.

    Custom view classes
    ###################

    The :class:`View` class can be inherited from to define additional properties or methods on
    a view. The only two names that are reserved on instances of :class:`View` are :meth:`as_value`
    and :meth:`eq`, leaving the rest to the developer. The :class:`Struct` and :class:`Union`
    classes provided in this module are subclasses of :class:`View` that also provide a concise way
    to define a layout.
    """
    def __init__(self, layout, target):
        try:
            cast_layout = Layout.cast(layout)
        except TypeError as e:
            raise TypeError("View layout must be a layout, not {!r}"
                            .format(layout)) from e
        try:
            cast_target = Value.cast(target)
        except TypeError as e:
            raise TypeError("View target must be a value-castable object, not {!r}"
                            .format(target)) from e
        if len(cast_target) != cast_layout.size:
            raise ValueError("View target is {} bit(s) wide, which is not compatible with "
                             "the {} bit(s) wide view layout"
                             .format(len(cast_target), cast_layout.size))
        for name, field in cast_layout:
            if isinstance(name, str) and name[0] != "_" and hasattr(type(self), name):
                warnings.warn("View layout includes a field {!r} that will be shadowed by "
                              "the view attribute '{}.{}.{}'"
                              .format(name, type(self).__module__, type(self).__qualname__, name),
                              SyntaxWarning, stacklevel=2)
        self.__orig_layout = layout
        self.__layout = cast_layout
        self.__target = cast_target

    def shape(self):
        """Get layout of this view.

        Returns
        -------
        :class:`Layout`
            The ``layout`` provided when constructing the view.
        """
        return self.__orig_layout

    def as_value(self):
        """Get underlying value.

        Returns
        -------
        :class:`Value`
            The ``target`` provided when constructing the view, or the :class:`Signal` that
            was created.
        """
        return self.__target

    def eq(self, other):
        """Assign to the underlying value.

        Returns
        -------
        :class:`Assign`
            ``self.as_value().eq(other)``
        """
        return self.as_value().eq(other)

    def __getitem__(self, key):
        """Slice the underlying value.

        A field corresponding to ``key`` is looked up in the layout. If the field's shape is
        a shape-castable object that has a ``__call__`` method, it is called and the result is
        returned. Otherwise, ``as_shape`` is called repeatedly on the shape until either an object
        with a ``__call__`` method is reached, or a ``Shape`` is returned. In the latter case,
        returns an unspecified Amaranth expression with the right shape.

        Arguments
        ---------
        key : :class:`str` or :class:`int` or :class:`ValueCastable`
            Name or index of a field.

        Returns
        -------
        :class:`Value` or :class:`ValueCastable`, inout
            A slice of the underlying value defined by the field.

        Raises
        ------
        KeyError
            If the layout does not define a field corresponding to ``key``.
        TypeError
            If ``key`` is a value-castable object, but the layout of the view is not
            a :class:`ArrayLayout`.
        TypeError
            If ``ShapeCastable.__call__`` does not return a value or a value-castable object.
        """
        if isinstance(self.__layout, ArrayLayout):
            if not isinstance(key, (int, Value, ValueCastable)):
                raise TypeError("Views with array layout may only be indexed with an integer "
                                "or a value, not {!r}"
                                .format(key))
            shape = self.__layout.elem_shape
            value = self.__target.word_select(key, Shape.cast(self.__layout.elem_shape).width)
        else:
            if isinstance(key, (Value, ValueCastable)):
                raise TypeError("Only views with array layout, not {!r}, may be indexed "
                                "with a value"
                                .format(self.__layout))
            field = self.__layout[key]
            shape = field.shape
            value = self.__target[field.offset:field.offset + field.width]
        # Field guarantees that the shape-castable object is well-formed, so there is no need
        # to handle erroneous cases here.
        if isinstance(shape, ShapeCastable):
            value = shape(value)
            if not isinstance(value, (Value, ValueCastable)):
                raise TypeError("{!r}.__call__() must return a value or "
                                "a value-castable object, not {!r}"
                                .format(shape, value))
            return value
        if Shape.cast(shape).signed:
            return value.as_signed()
        else:
            return value

    def __getattr__(self, name):
        """Access a field of the underlying value.

        Returns ``self[name]``.

        Raises
        ------
        AttributeError
            If the layout does not define a field called ``name``, or if ``name`` starts with
            an underscore.
        """
        if isinstance(self.__layout, ArrayLayout):
            raise AttributeError("View of {!r} with an array layout does not have fields"
                                 .format(self.__target))
        try:
            item = self[name]
        except KeyError:
            raise AttributeError("View of {!r} does not have a field {!r}; "
                                 "did you mean one of: {}?"
                                 .format(self.__target, name,
                                         ", ".join(repr(name)
                                                   for name, field in self.__layout)))
        if name.startswith("_"):
            raise AttributeError("View of {!r} field {!r} has a reserved name and may only be "
                                 "accessed by indexing"
                                 .format(self.__target, name))
        return item

    def __eq__(self, other):
        if not isinstance(other, View) or self.__layout != other.__layout:
            raise TypeError(f"View of {self.__layout!r} can only be compared to another view of the same layout, not {other!r}")
        return self.__target == other.__target

    def __ne__(self, other):
        if not isinstance(other, View) or self.__layout != other.__layout:
            raise TypeError(f"View of {self.__layout!r} can only be compared to another view of the same layout, not {other!r}")
        return self.__target != other.__target

    def __add__(self, other):
        raise TypeError("Cannot perform arithmetic operations on a View")

    __radd__ = __add__
    __sub__ = __add__
    __rsub__ = __add__
    __mul__ = __add__
    __rmul__ = __add__
    __floordiv__ = __add__
    __rfloordiv__ = __add__
    __mod__ = __add__
    __rmod__ = __add__
    __lshift__ = __add__
    __rlshift__ = __add__
    __rshift__ = __add__
    __rrshift__ = __add__
    __lt__ = __add__
    __le__ = __add__
    __gt__ = __add__
    __ge__ = __add__

    def __and__(self, other):
        raise TypeError("Cannot perform bitwise operations on a View")

    __rand__ = __and__
    __or__ = __and__
    __ror__ = __and__
    __xor__ = __and__
    __rxor__ = __and__

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"{self.__class__.__name__}({self.__layout!r}, {self.__target!r})"


class _AggregateMeta(ShapeCastable, type):
    def __new__(metacls, name, bases, namespace):
        if "__annotations__" not in namespace:
            # This is a base class without its own layout. It is not shape-castable, and cannot
            # be instantiated. It can be used to share behavior.
            return type.__new__(metacls, name, bases, namespace)
        elif all(not hasattr(base, "_AggregateMeta__layout") for base in bases):
            # This is a leaf class with its own layout. It is shape-castable and can
            # be instantiated. It can also be subclassed, and used to share layout and behavior.
            layout  = dict()
            default = dict()
            for name in {**namespace["__annotations__"]}:
                try:
                    Shape.cast(namespace["__annotations__"][name])
                except TypeError:
                    # Not a shape-castable annotation; leave as-is.
                    continue
                layout[name] = namespace["__annotations__"].pop(name)
                if name in namespace:
                    default[name] = namespace.pop(name)
            cls = type.__new__(metacls, name, bases, namespace)
            if cls.__layout_cls is UnionLayout:
                if len(default) > 1:
                    raise ValueError("Initial value for at most one field can be provided for "
                                     "a union class (specified: {})"
                                     .format(", ".join(default.keys())))
            cls.__layout  = cls.__layout_cls(layout)
            cls.__default = default
            return cls
        else:
            # This is a class that has a base class with a layout and annotations. Such a class
            # is not well-formed.
            raise TypeError("Aggregate class '{}' must either inherit or specify a layout, "
                            "not both"
                            .format(name))

    def as_shape(cls):
        if not hasattr(cls, "_AggregateMeta__layout"):
            raise TypeError("Aggregate class '{}.{}' does not have a defined shape"
                            .format(cls.__module__, cls.__qualname__))
        return cls.__layout

    def __call__(cls, target):
        # This method exists to pass the override check done by ShapeCastable.
        return super().__call__(cls, target)

    def const(cls, init):
        if cls.__layout_cls is UnionLayout:
            if init is not None and len(init) > 1:
                raise ValueError("Initializer for at most one field can be provided for "
                                 "a union class (specified: {})"
                                 .format(", ".join(init.keys())))
            return cls.as_shape().const(init or cls.__default)
        else:
            fields = cls.__default.copy()
            fields.update(init or {})
            return cls.as_shape().const(fields)

    def _value_repr(cls, value):
        return cls.__layout._value_repr(value)


class Struct(View, metaclass=_AggregateMeta):
    """Structures defined with annotations.

    The :class:`Struct` base class is a subclass of :class:`View` that provides a concise way
    to describe the structure layout and initial values for the fields using Python
    :term:`variable annotations <python:variable annotation>`.

    Any annotations containing :ref:`shape-like <lang-shapelike>` objects are used,
    in the order in which they appear in the source code, to construct a :class:`StructLayout`.
    The values assigned to such annotations are used to populate the initial value of the signal
    created by the view. Any other annotations are kept as-is.

    .. testsetup::

        from amaranth import *
        from amaranth.lib.data import *

    As an example, a structure for `IEEE 754 single-precision floating-point format
    <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-precision_floating-point_format>`_ can be defined as:

    .. testcode::

        class IEEE754Single(Struct):
            fraction: 23
            exponent:  8 = 0x7f
            sign:      1

            def is_subnormal(self):
                return self.exponent == 0

    The ``IEEE754Single`` class itself can be used where a :ref:`shape <lang-shapes>` is expected:

    .. doctest::

        >>> IEEE754Single.as_shape()
        StructLayout({'fraction': 23, 'exponent': 8, 'sign': 1})
        >>> Signal(IEEE754Single).as_value().width
        32

    Instances of this class can be used where :ref:`values <lang-values>` are expected:

    .. doctest::

        >>> flt = Signal(IEEE754Single)
        >>> Signal(32).eq(flt)
        (eq (sig $signal) (sig flt))

    Accessing shape-castable properties returns slices of the underlying value:

    .. doctest::

        >>> flt.fraction
        (slice (sig flt) 0:23)
        >>> flt.is_subnormal()
        (== (slice (sig flt) 23:31) (const 1'd0))

    The initial values for individual fields can be overridden during instantiation:

    .. doctest::

        >>> hex(Signal(IEEE754Single).as_value().init)
        '0x3f800000'
        >>> hex(Signal(IEEE754Single, init={'sign': 1}).as_value().init)
        '0xbf800000'
        >>> hex(Signal(IEEE754Single, init={'exponent': 0}).as_value().init)
        '0x0'

    Classes inheriting from :class:`Struct` can be used as base classes. The only restrictions
    are that:

    * Classes that do not define a layout cannot be instantiated or converted to a shape;
    * A layout can be defined exactly once in the inheritance hierarchy.

    Behavior can be shared through inheritance:

    .. testcode::

        class HasChecksum(Struct):
            def checksum(self):
                bits = Value.cast(self)
                return sum(bits[n:n+8] for n in range(0, len(bits), 8))

        class BareHeader(HasChecksum):
            address: 16
            length:   8

        class HeaderWithParam(HasChecksum):
            address: 16
            length:   8
            param:    8

    .. doctest::

        >>> HasChecksum.as_shape()
        Traceback (most recent call last):
          ...
        TypeError: Aggregate class 'HasChecksum' does not have a defined shape
        >>> bare = Signal(BareHeader); bare.checksum()
        (+ (+ (+ (const 1'd0) (slice (sig bare) 0:8)) (slice (sig bare) 8:16)) (slice (sig bare) 16:24))
        >>> param = Signal(HeaderWithParam); param.checksum()
        (+ (+ (+ (+ (const 1'd0) (slice (sig param) 0:8)) (slice (sig param) 8:16)) (slice (sig param) 16:24)) (slice (sig param) 24:32))
    """
    _AggregateMeta__layout_cls = StructLayout


class Union(View, metaclass=_AggregateMeta):
    """Unions defined with annotations.

    The :class:`Union` base class is a subclass of :class:`View` that provides a concise way
    to describe the union layout using Python :term:`variable annotations <python:variable
    annotation>`. It is very similar to the :class:`Struct` class, except that its layout
    is a :class:`UnionLayout`.

        >>> Signal(VarInt).as_value().init
        256
        >>> Signal(VarInt, init={'int8': 10}).as_value().init
        10
    """
    _AggregateMeta__layout_cls = UnionLayout

198: class ShapeCastable:
199:     """Interface class for objects that can be cast to a :class:`Shape`.
200: 
201:     Shapes of values in the Amaranth language are specified using :ref:`shape-like objects
202:     <lang-shapelike>`. Inheriting a class from :class:`ShapeCastable` and implementing all of
203:     the methods described below adds instances of that class to the list of shape-like objects
204:     recognized by the :meth:`Shape.cast` method. This is a part of the mechanism for seamlessly
205:     extending the Amaranth language in third-party code.
206: 
207:     To illustrate their purpose, consider constructing a signal from a shape-castable object
208:     :py:`shape_castable`:
209: 
210:     .. code::
211: 
212:         value_like = Signal(shape_castable, init=initializer)
213: 
214:     The code above is equivalent to:
215: 
216:     .. code::
217: 
218:         value_like = shape_castable(Signal(
219:             shape_castable.as_shape(),
220:             init=shape_castable.const(initializer)
221:         ))
222: 
223:     Note that the :py:`shape_castable(x)` syntax performs :py:`shape_castable.__call__(x)`.
224: 
225:     .. tip::
226: 
227:         The source code of the :mod:`amaranth.lib.data` module can be used as a reference for
228:         implementing a fully featured shape-castable object.
229:     """
230: 
231:     def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
232:         if type(self) is ShapeCastable:
233:             raise TypeError("Can't instantiate abstract class ShapeCastable")
234:         super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
235: 
236:     def __init_subclass__(cls, **kwargs):
237:         if cls.as_shape is ShapeCastable.as_shape:
238:             raise TypeError(f"Class '{cls.__name__}' deriving from 'ShapeCastable' must override "
239:                             f"the 'as_shape' method")
240:         if cls.const is ShapeCastable.const:
241:             raise TypeError(f"Class '{cls.__name__}' deriving from 'ShapeCastable' must override "
242:                             f"the 'const' method")
243:         if cls.__call__ is ShapeCastable.__call__:
244:             raise TypeError(f"Class '{cls.__name__}' deriving from 'ShapeCastable' must override "
245:                             f"the '__call__' method")
246: 
247:     # The signatures and definitions of these methods are weird because they are present here for
248:     # documentation (and error checking above) purpose only and should not affect control flow.
249:     # This especially applies to `__call__`, where subclasses may call `super().__call__()` in
250:     # creative ways.
251: 
252:     def as_shape(self, *args, **kwargs):
253:         """as_shape()
254: 
255:         Convert :py:`self` to a :ref:`shape-like object <lang-shapelike>`.
256: 
257:         This method is called by the Amaranth language to convert :py:`self` to a concrete
258:         :class:`Shape`. It will usually return a :class:`Shape` object, but it may also return
259:         another shape-like object to delegate its functionality.
260: 
261:         This method must be idempotent: when called twice on the same object, the result must be
262:         exactly the same.
263: 
264:         This method may also be called by code that is not a part of the Amaranth language.
265: 
266:         Returns
267:         -------
268:         Any other object recognized by :meth:`Shape.cast`.
269: 
270:         Raises
271:         ------
272:         Exception
273:             When the conversion cannot be done. This exception must be propagated by callers
274:             (except when checking whether an object is shape-castable or not), either directly
275:             or as a cause of another exception.
276:         """
277:         return super().as_shape(*args, **kwargs) # :nocov:
278: 
279:     def const(self, *args, **kwargs):
280:         """const(obj)
281: 
282:         Convert a constant initializer :py:`obj` to its value representation.
283: 
284:         This method is called by the Amaranth language to convert :py:`obj`, which may be an
285:         arbitrary Python object, to a concrete :ref:`value-like object <lang-valuelike>`.
286:         The object :py:`obj` will usually be a Python literal that can conveniently represent
287:         a constant value whose shape is described by :py:`self`. While not constrained here,
288:         the result will usually be an instance of the return type of :meth:`__call__`.
289: 
290:         For any :py:`obj`, the following condition must hold:
291: 
292:         .. code::
293: 
294:             Shape.cast(self) == Const.cast(self.const(obj)).shape()
295: 
296:         This method may also be called by code that is not a part of the Amaranth language.
297: 
298:         Returns
299:         -------
300:         A :ref:`value-like object <lang-valuelike>` that is :ref:`constant-castable <lang-constcasting>`.
301: 
302:         Raises
303:         ------
304:         Exception
305:             When the conversion cannot be done. This exception must be propagated by callers,
306:             either directly or as a cause of another exception. While not constrained here,
307:             usually the exception class will be :exc:`TypeError` or :exc:`ValueError`.
308:         """
309:         return super().const(*args, **kwargs) # :nocov:
310: 
311:     def __call__(self, *args, **kwargs):
312:         """__call__(obj)
313: 
314:         Lift a :ref:`value-like object <lang-valuelike>` to a higher-level representation.
315: 
316:         This method is called by the Amaranth language to lift :py:`obj`, which may be any
317:         :ref:`value-like object <lang-valuelike>` whose shape equals :py:`Shape.cast(self)`,
318:         to a higher-level representation, which may be any value-like object with the same
319:         shape. While not constrained here, usually a :class:`ShapeCastable` implementation will
320:         be paired with a :class:`ValueCastable` implementation, and this method will return
321:         an instance of the latter.
322: 
323:         If :py:`obj` is not as described above, this interface does not constrain the behavior
324:         of this method. This may be used to implement another call-based protocol at the same
325:         time.
326: 
327:         For any compliant :py:`obj`, the following condition must hold:
328: 
329:         .. code::
330: 
331:             Value.cast(self(obj)) == Value.cast(obj)
332: 
333:         This method may also be called by code that is not a part of the Amaranth language.
334: 
335:         Returns
336:         -------
337:         A :ref:`value-like object <lang-valuelike>`.
338:         """
339:         return super().__call__(*args, **kwargs) # :nocov:
340: 
341:     # TODO: write an RFC for turning this into a proper interface method
342:     def _value_repr(self, value):
343:         return (_repr.Repr(_repr.FormatInt(), value),)

356:             for member in instance:

391: def _overridable_by_reflected(method_name):
392:     """Allow overriding the decorated method.
393: 
394:     Allows :class:`ValueCastable` to override the decorated method by implementing
395:     a reflected method named ``method_name``. Intended for operators, but
396:     also usable for other methods that have a reflected counterpart.
397:     """
398:     def decorator(f):
399:         @functools.wraps(f)
400:         def wrapper(self, other):
401:             if isinstance(other, ValueCastable) and hasattr(other, method_name):
402:                 res = getattr(other, method_name)(self)
403:                 if res is not NotImplemented:
404:                     return res
405:             return f(self, other)
406:         return wrapper
407:     return decorator

410: class Value(metaclass=ABCMeta):
411:     """Abstract representation of a bit pattern computed in a circuit.
412: 
413:     The Amaranth language gives Python code the ability to create a circuit netlist by manipulating
414:     objects representing the computations within that circuit. The :class:`Value` class represents
415:     the bit pattern of a constant, or of a circuit input or output, or within a storage element; or
416:     the result of an arithmetic, logical, or bit container operation.
417: 
418:     Operations on this class interpret this bit pattern either as an integer, which can be signed
419:     or unsigned depending on the value's :meth:`shape`, or as a bit container. In either case,
420:     the semantics of operations that implement Python's syntax, like :py:`+` (also known as
421:     :meth:`__add__`), are identical to the corresponding operation on a Python :class:`int` (or on
422:     a Python sequence container). The bitwise inversion :py:`~` (also known as :meth:`__invert__`)
423:     is the sole exception to this rule.
424: 
425:     Data that is not conveniently representable by a single integer or a bit container can be
426:     represented by wrapping a :class:`Value` in a :class:`ValueCastable` subclass that provides
427:     domain-specific operations. It is possible to extend Amaranth in third-party code using
428:     value-castable objects, and the Amaranth standard library provides several built-in ones:
429: 
430:     * :mod:`amaranth.lib.enum` classes are a drop-in replacement for the standard Python
431:       :class:`enum` classes that can be defined with an Amaranth shape;
432:     * :mod:`amaranth.lib.data` classes allow defining complex data structures such as structures
433:       and unions.
434: 
435:     Operations on :class:`Value` instances return another :class:`Value` instance. Unless the exact
436:     type and value of the result is explicitly specified below, it should be considered opaque, and
437:     may change without notice between Amaranth releases as long as the semantics remains the same.
438: 
439:     .. note::
440: 
441:         In each of the descriptions below, you will see a line similar to:
442: 
443:         **Return type:** :class:`Value`, :py:`unsigned(1)`, :ref:`assignable <lang-assignable>`
444: 
445:         The first part (:class:`Value`) indicates that the returned object's type is a subclass
446:         of :class:`Value`. The second part (:py:`unsigned(1)`) describes the shape of that value.
447:         The third part, if present, indicates that the value is assignable if :py:`self` is
448:         assignable.
449:     """
450: 
451:     @staticmethod
452:     def cast(obj):
453:         """Cast :py:`obj` to an Amaranth value.
454: 
455:         Many :ref:`value-like <lang-valuelike>` objects can be cast to a value:
456: 
457:         * a :class:`Value` instance, where the result is itself;
458:         * a :class:`bool` or :class:`int` instance, where the result is :py:`Const(obj)`;
459:         * an :class:`enum.IntEnum` instance, or a :class:`enum.Enum` instance whose members are
460:           all integers, where the result is a :class:`Const(obj, enum_shape)` where :py:`enum_shape`
461:           is a shape that can represent every member of the enumeration;
462:         * a :class:`ValueCastable` instance, where the result is obtained by repeatedly calling
463:           :meth:`obj.as_value() <ValueCastable.as_value>`.

465:         Raises
466:         ------
467:         TypeError
468:             If :py:`obj` cannot be converted to a :class:`Value`.
469:         RecursionError
470:             If :py:`obj` is a :class:`ValueCastable` object that casts to itself.
471:         """
472:         while True:
473:             if isinstance(obj, Value):

475:             elif isinstance(obj, ValueCastable):

477:             elif isinstance(obj, Enum):

479:             elif isinstance(obj, int):
480:                 return Const(obj)
481:             else:
482:                 raise TypeError(f"Object {obj!r} cannot be converted to an Amaranth value")
483:             if new_obj is obj:
484:                 raise RecursionError(f"Value-castable object {obj!r} casts to itself")

1181:     def matches(self, *patterns):
1182:         """Pattern matching.

1195:         # This code should accept exactly the same patterns as `with m.Case(...):`.
1196:         for pattern in patterns:
1197:             if isinstance(pattern, str) and any(bit not in "01- \t" for bit in pattern):
1198:                 raise SyntaxError("Match pattern '{}' must consist of 0, 1, and - (don't care) "
1199:                                   "bits, and may include whitespace"
1200:                                   .format(pattern))
1201:             if (isinstance(pattern, str) and
1202:                     len("".join(pattern.split())) != len(self)):
1203:                 raise SyntaxError("Match pattern '{}' must have the same width as match value "
1204:                                   "(which is {})"
1205:                                   .format(pattern, len(self)))
1206:             if isinstance(pattern, str):
1207:                 pattern = "".join(pattern.split()) # remove whitespace
1208:                 mask    = int(pattern.replace("0", "1").replace("-", "0"), 2)
1209:                 pattern = int(pattern.replace("-", "0"), 2)
1210:                 matches.append((self & mask) == pattern)
1211:             else:

1216:                                       "expression, not {!r}"
1217:                                       .format(pattern)) from e
1218:                 pattern_len = bits_for(pattern.value)
